methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series C → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.7x) to $380M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Transportation (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 3 same-sector peers exist in Transportation, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
ZeroAvia is a Series C stage transportation company founded by Valery Miftakhov that has raised $380M+ to date. The transportation sector peer set comprises 7 private companies, including Rivian, The Boring Company, Einride, Slate Auto, and Harbinger. No public comparables exist in this narrow segment.

The valuation analysis applies a stage-progression methodology, the only triangulation method yielding sufficient data. Using total capital raised ($380M) as a baseline valuation proxy and applying a typical Series C-to-next-stage step-up multiplier of 1.7x, this approach implies a post-money valuation of $646M. The peer-median method is not applicable due to insufficient same-stage and adjacent-stage comparables within the transportation sector; the three available peers lack the concentration required for reliable median benchmarking.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $549M to $743M, with a median point of $646M. This range reflects approximately ±15% variance around the stage-progression estimate. Key uncertainties include the absence of tight-peer public market data to calibrate multiples, the reliance on a single methodology, and potential variation in how total raised translates to fair post-money value at this stage. The narrow peer universe limits the robustness of cross-checks and warrants sensitivity analysis around the 1.7x multiplier assumption.
